title: Interview: John Lennon for Trinidad Express | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono gave an interview to the Trinidad Express newspaper on 29 April 1971.

They had flown from London to Arima in Trinidad on 26 April. The main purpose of their visit was to see Michael X and his family. Michael X, born Michael de Freitas in Trinidad in 1933, was an activist also known as Michael Abdul Malik and Abdul Malik.

Lennon and Ono were interviewed by Raoul Pantin of the Trinidad Express at their hotel, Hassina’s, at 26 Christina Gardens in Arima. They discussed Lennon’s history with The Beatles, his drug use, and future plans.

I’ve been playing musical instruments from the age of eight onwards, I could never give it up. But what I’m less and less interested in is standing on a stage like a performing flea. And although I still have that urge, I still have the feelings of my life with me, I’m more inclined now to be a 20th century writer, which is to put my writing on wax and send it out.
John Lennon
